plausibility_review.reason: The proposed organization creates a significant human-manageability risk on Wednesday by scheduling an immediate departure at the exact end of post-night-shift sleep and then a dense 15:30–22:00 chain before another early hospital day. The plan may technically fit and it does protect sleep duration, but it gives little evidence that the user can realistically wake, prepare, travel, attend physiotherapy, join an online meeting, eat late, and complete focused thesis work without practical margin after overnight clinical work.
plausibility_review.suggested_improvement: Reconsider the Wednesday distribution with the fuller context, especially the immediate transition from post-night-shift sleep to physiotherapy and the fully chained late-afternoon/evening sequence. If the same operations are kept, provide grounded support for why the exact transitions, late lunch, and post-night-shift cognitive workload are acceptable for this user.

unresolved_assumptions.assumption: The user can tolerate delaying Wednesday lunch until 18:00 after the night shift, daytime sleep, physiotherapy and supervisor meeting.

weaknesses: Wednesday is extremely compressed after the night shift: hospital shift 2026-11-17 23:00–2026-11-18 07:00, commute home 07:00–07:30, sleep 07:30–15:30, then immediate commute to physiotherapy 15:30–15:45 with no visible wake-up, hygiene, food, preparation or recovery margin.

The plan protects an intact eight-hour sleep block, but it treats the exact end of sleep as immediately usable time for leaving home. That may be technically valid but is a practical human-quality risk after overnight hospital work.

The post-sleep Wednesday sequence runs without meaningful slack from 15:30 to 22:00: commute to physiotherapy, physiotherapy 15:45–16:45, commute home 16:45–17:00, supervisor meeting 17:00–18:00, lunch 18:00–19:00, thesis work 19:00–21:00, dinner 21:00–22:00, then protected sleep 22:00–06:00 before Thursday work. This may preserve priorities on paper while leaving little resilience if any item overruns or the user is fatigued.

Lunch is moved to 18:00 on Wednesday, after a night shift, daytime sleep, physiotherapy travel/session, and supervisor meeting. The rationale acknowledges late meals but does not explain whether this is practically sustainable for the user on a post-night-shift day.

The supervisor meeting at 17:00 starts exactly when the commute home from physiotherapy ends. Because it is online and at home this may be possible, but the calendar leaves no visible setup or decompression time.

Moving Wednesday swimming to Friday 18:00–20:00 may be sensible, but the rationale itself says this depends on no unseen Friday commitment and returned day off; the visible calendar does not establish that Friday is otherwise manageable.

Several external confirmations remain unresolved: physiotherapy availability, supervisor acceptance, HR or ward manager swap record, Friday day off, and pool availability. These are not technical violations, but they are central to whether the proposed routine can actually happen.
prior_critic_reviews.feedback: The proposal has a reasonable priority structure: it protects the night-shift recovery sleep, preserves physiotherapy, keeps the supervisor meeting and thesis work, and moves lower-priority swimming away from the most compressed part of Wednesday. However, the resulting Wednesday is only barely human-shaped. The main issue is not an overlap; it is the reliance on exact back-to-back use of time after an overnight hospital shift. The user would finish work at 07:00, get home at 07:30, sleep until 15:30, and immediately leave for physiotherapy, then continue through meeting, delayed lunch, thesis work, dinner and another protected sleep block. That may be feasible for a very resilient person with everything prepared in advance, but the rationale does not substantiate that level of precision or recovery capacity. A revision should reconsider whether the post-night-shift Wednesday needs more practical margin, or provide a grounded explanation from the fuller context for why the immediate wake-to-physio and continuous evening sequence is acceptable. The original request cannot be independently verified from the provided material, so this review is limited to the visible proposal, rationale, resulting calendar and validation report.

rationale.summary: The plan records the night-shift swap, rebuilds the hospital commutes, protects full recovery sleep, and makes Wednesday less brittle by moving physiotherapy to Thursday with confirmation. The main trade-off is dropping one swim and moving another to Friday so recovery, thesis work, the supervisor meeting and health care can all remain plausible.
